title: David Hears Some Crazy News
paragraphs: So, right after Saul died, David got back to Ziklag from totally crushing the Amalekites. Then, three days later, this random guy shows up from Saul’s army camp.
Dude was a mess, obviously mourning, and he got on his knees to show respect to David. David’s like, “What brings you here?”
He answered, “I literally just escaped from the Israelite camp.”
“So what happened?” David asked. “Give me the full story.”
He said, “The Israelite army ran from the battle, leaving a bunch of their dead friends behind. And get this—Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
David pressed the young soldier for the details: “How are you so sure Saul and Jonathan are dead?”

“I just happened to be on Mount Gilboa and saw Saul, super messed up and leaning on his spear, with enemy chariots and horsemen closing in on him, for real. He looked back, saw me, and called me over. I was like, ‘Yes sir, at your service.’ He asked who I was, and I told him, ‘I’m an Amalekite.’”
“‘Come here,’ he said, ‘and put me out of my misery. I’m as good as dead, just hanging on.’”
“So I did what he asked—I killed him. I knew he wasn’t going to last much longer anyway. I took his royal headband and bracelet and brought them to my master. Here they are.”

David was so devastated he ripped his clothes to shreds. All the men with him did the same. They cried and fasted for the rest of the day, grieving for Saul and his son Jonathan, and also for God’s army and the nation of Israel, all victims in a failed battle.
Then David looked at the young soldier who brought the report: “Who are you, for real?”
“I’m from an immigrant family—an Amalekite.”
“Are you serious?” said David. “You weren’t afraid to just up and kill God’s anointed king?” He immediately ordered one of his soldiers, “Strike him dead!” The soldier struck him, and he died.
“You asked for it,” David told him. “You sealed your own death sentence when you said you killed God’s anointed king.”
Then David sang this lament for Saul and his son Jonathan, and ordered that everyone in Judah learn it by heart. Yeah, it’s even written in The Book of Jashar.

Oh, the gazelles of Israel, struck down on your hills, the mighty warriors—fallen, just fallen! Don’t talk about it in the city of Gath, don’t post the news in the streets of Ashkelon. Don’t give those Philistine girls another reason to party. No more dew or rain for you, hills of Gilboa, not a drop from the springs, because that’s where the warriors’ shields were dragged through the mud, Saul’s shield left there to rot.
Jonathan’s bow was legendary—the bigger they were, the harder they fell. Saul’s sword was fearless—once it was out, nothing could stop it.
Saul and Jonathan—so loved, so awesome! Together in life, together in death. Faster than eagles, stronger than lions.

Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He dressed you in the finest clothes and silks, spared no expense to make you look good. The mighty warriors—fallen, fallen in the middle of the fight! Jonathan—struck down on your hills!
Oh my dear brother Jonathan, I’m crushed by your death. Your friendship was a miracle, for real—a love way beyond anything I’ve ever known, or ever hope to know.
The mighty warriors—fallen, fallen. And their weapons of war, broken to pieces.

title: Civil War STARTS! David vs. Saul's Son
paragraphs: So after all that went down, David hit up God. He was like, 'Yo, should I roll out to one of the cities in Judah?' And God was straight up, 'Yep, time to move.' David asked, 'Aight, which one?' God said, 'Hebron.'

So David packed up and moved to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, who used to be married to Nabal from Carmel. All of David's crew and their families came with and they all settled down in and around Hebron.
The people of Judah showed up in Hebron and, right then and there, they crowned David king over all the clans of Judah. It was official.

Then David got word that the guys from Jabesh Gilead had given Saul a proper funeral. David sent messengers to them, saying, 'God bless you guys for honoring your old leader, Saul, like that. Seriously, may God be good to you, and I'll do the same. I'll match that kindness you showed. Now, be strong and ready for what's next. Your master Saul is dead, and the people of Judah have made me their king.'

Meanwhile, Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul’s army, took Saul’s son Ish-Bosheth to Mahanaim and made him king over Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, Benjamin—basically, he tried to make him king over all of Israel. Ish-Bosheth was 40 when this happened, but his reign only lasted two years. The tribe of Judah, though, was loyal to David. David ruled Judah from Hebron for seven and a half years.

One day, Abner son of Ner and the soldiers of Ish-Bosheth marched out from Mahanaim to Gibeon. Joab son of Zeruiah, with David’s soldiers, also set out. The two groups met at the Pool of Gibeon and faced off, one on each side of the pool.
Abner called out to Joab, 'Let's have your best guys fight. Let's see what they've got.'
Joab shot back, 'You're on! Let's do it!'

So they got ready to throw down. Twelve Benjaminites for Ish-Bosheth, and twelve of David's soldiers. It was wild—each guy grabbed his opponent's head and stabbed him with a sword. They all died right there, the whole group together. So they named the place 'Slaughter Park,' and it's right there in Gibeon.

The battle got super intense after that. Abner and the men of Israel got totally crushed by David's crew. The three sons of Zeruiah—Joab, Abishai, and Asahel—were there. Asahel was crazy fast, like a gazelle, and he started chasing Abner, sticking right on his tail.
Abner looked back and yelled, 'Asahel, is that you?'
'You know it!' Asahel yelled back.
Abner warned him, 'Back off, dude. Go pick a fight with someone you can actually beat and take their stuff!' But Asahel was relentless and wouldn't stop.
Abner tried again, 'Seriously, turn back! Don't make me kill you. How could I ever face your brother Joab if I did?'

But he wouldn't quit, so Abner jabbed him in the stomach with the butt end of his spear. He hit him so hard it went right through his back. Asahel dropped and died right there. Everyone who came to that spot just stopped and stared at his body. But Joab and Abishai kept chasing after Abner. As the sun was setting, they reached the hill of Ammah, which faced Giah on the road to the backcountry of Gibeon. The Benjaminites had taken their stand with Abner there, spread out strategically on top of the hill.

But Joab and Abishai didn't stop; they kept chasing Abner. As the sun was setting, they got to the hill of Ammah. The soldiers of Benjamin had regrouped with Abner there, setting up a defensive position on the hill.
Abner yelled out to Joab, 'Are we just gonna keep fighting forever? Don't you get that this will only end badly for everyone? How long are you gonna keep chasing your own brothers?'

Joab replied, 'As God is my witness, if you hadn't said something, we would've kept this chase going all night!' Then Joab blew the trumpet, and the whole army stopped. They quit chasing the Israelites and the fighting was over.
Abner and his soldiers marched all night through the Arabah Valley. They crossed the Jordan River and, after a long march, finally got back to Mahanaim.

When Joab got back from chasing Abner, he did a headcount. Nineteen of David's men were missing, not including Asahel. But they had taken down 360 of Abner's men, all from the tribe of Benjamin—all dead. They took Asahel's body and buried him in his family's tomb in Bethlehem. Then Joab and his men marched through the night, arriving back in Hebron just as the sun came up.

title: The OG Beef: Betrayal and Revenge
paragraphs: The beef between Saul's crew and David's crew just kept going. But the longer it went, the stronger David's side got, while Saul's team was getting weaker and weaker.
While he was in Hebron, David had a bunch of sons:
Amnon was his first, from Ahinoam of Jezreel.
Kileab was his second, from Abigail of Carmel, who used to be married to Nabal.
Absalom was his third, from Maacah, who was the daughter of Talmai, the king of Geshur.
Adonijah was his fourth, from Haggith.
Shephatiah was his fifth, from Abital.
Ithream was his sixth, from Eglah.
So yeah, these six sons were all born in Hebron.

Abner, who was on Saul's side, was using the war to get more power for himself. Saul had a side-chick named Rizpah daughter of Aiah, and one day Saul's son Ish-Bosheth went off on Abner, like, "Why are you sleeping with my dad's girl?"

Abner totally lost it at Ish-Bosheth. "You think I'm some kind of dog? This is the thanks I get for being loyal to your dad's family and friends? I literally saved you from being captured by David, and you're gonna get mad at me for hooking up with a woman? You know what, I'm gonna help God make his promise to David come true. I'm gonna take the kingdom from Saul's family and make David the king of everyone, Israel and Judah, from Dan to Beersheba. If I don't, I hope God messes me up."
Ish-Bosheth was so scared by Abner's rant that he couldn't even say anything back.
So Abner sent messengers to David, saying, "Make a deal with me, and I'll get all of Israel on your side."
David was like, "Awesome, it's a deal. But on one condition: you have to bring back my wife Michal, Saul's daughter, when you come to see me."
Then David sent messengers to Ish-Bosheth, saying, "Give me back my wife Michal. I paid for her with a hundred Philistine foreskins."
Ish-Bosheth made her leave her husband, Paltiel son of Laish. But Paltiel followed her, crying the whole way, until they got to Bahurim. Then Abner told him, "Go home," and he did.

Abner got all the leaders of Israel together and said, "You guys were already trying to make David your king, right? Well, now's the time to do it! God even said he'd save Israel from the Philistines and all their enemies through David."
Abner also talked to the Benjaminites privately. Then he went to Hebron to talk to David and tell him everything Israel and Benjamin were planning.
When Abner and his twenty guys met David in Hebron, David threw a big party for them.

Then Abner said, "Alright, I'm ready. I'm gonna go rally everyone in Israel for you, my king. They'll make a deal with you, and you can rule them however you want." David sent him off with his blessing.

Right after that, David's men, led by Joab, came back from a mission. Abner son of Ner was already gone--he wasn't in Hebron with David anymore.When Joab and his crew got there, they were told that Abner had been there with David and had left on good terms.

Joab went straight to the king and was like, "What did you just do? Abner shows up, and you just let him go? You know Abner son of Ner—he wasn't here to be friends. He was here to spy on you and figure out what you're up to."

Joab left David and immediately sent messengers after Abner. They caught up with him at the well at Sirah and brought him back. David had no idea. When Abner got back to Hebron, Joab pulled him aside at the gate to talk privately. And then he stabbed him in the stomach and killed him, to get revenge for his brother Asahel's death.

When David heard what happened, he said, "God knows that my kingdom and I are innocent of the murder of Abner son of Ner. Joab and his whole family will be cursed for this. I hope they're always dealing with sickness, violence, and hunger." (Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel at the battle of Gibeon.)

David told Joab and all his men, "Tear your clothes, wear mourning clothes, and lead Abner's funeral, crying loudly." King David even followed the coffin. They buried Abner in Hebron, and the king cried super loudly at his grave. Everyone else was crying too.
Then the king sang this song for Abner:
"How can this be? Abner's dead like some random dude? You were a free man, you could do whatever you wanted—but you got taken out in a street fight."
And everyone started crying even harder.

Then they all tried to get David to eat something before it got dark. But David swore, "I swear to God, I won't eat anything, not even a piece of bread, before the sun sets." Everyone there saw it and was impressed. Actually, everything the king did, the people loved. It was obvious to everyone that day, including all of Israel, that the king had nothing to do with the murder of Abner son of Ner.

The king said to his servants, "You guys realize that a prince and a hero was killed today, right? And even though I'm the king, I was powerless to stop it. These sons of Zeruiah are too much for me. God will pay back the criminal for his crime!"

title: Two Bros Betray Their King & Get What They Deserve
paragraphs: When Saul's son, Ish-Bosheth, heard that Abner had died in Hebron, he was devastated. His courage just evaporated, and the whole country was shook.

Now, Ish-Bosheth had these two guys, Baanah and Recab, who were captains of his raiding parties. They were sons of a dude named Rimmon from Beeroth, from the tribe of Benjamin. (A little backstory: the people of Beeroth had to dip and ended up in Gittaim, where they still live as foreigners).

Also, quick side note: Saul's son, Jonathan, had a son who couldn't use his feet. When he was five, the news about Saul and Jonathan's death came from Jezreel. His nanny grabbed him and ran, but in her panic, she dropped him, and he was injured permanently. His name was Mephibosheth.

So one day, Baanah and Recab, the two sons of Rimmon, headed over to Ish-Bosheth's house. They got there during the hottest part of the day, right when he was taking his afternoon nap. They got in by pretending they were there on official business. The guard at his bedroom door had dozed off, so they slipped right past her and went into the room where Ish-Bosheth was sleeping. They killed him, cut off his head, and took it as a trophy. They traveled all night through the Arabah Valley.

They brought Ish-Bosheth's head to David in Hebron and said, "Here's the head of Ish-Bosheth, son of your enemy Saul. He wanted to kill you, but today God has given you revenge on Saul and his family!"

David looked at the brothers, Recab and Baanah, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said, "As surely as God lives—the God who has saved me from all my troubles—when a guy brought me the news that Saul was dead, thinking I'd be thrilled, I had him arrested and killed right there in Ziklag. That was his reward for the 'good news.' And now you two, a couple of evil men, have murdered an innocent man in his own bed. You really think I won't hold you accountable for this murder and get rid of you?"

Then David gave the order to his soldiers. They killed the two brothers, chopped off their hands and feet, and hung their bodies up by the pool in Hebron. But they took Ish-Bosheth's head and buried it in Abner's tomb in Hebron.

title: David's Ultimate Glow-Up: Finally King of ALL Israel!
paragraphs: So after a bit, all the tribes of Israel went to David over in Hebron and were like, “Yo, look at us—we’re your own flesh and blood! Back when Saul was our king, you were the one actually leading us. And God even told you, ‘You’re gonna shepherd my people Israel and be their leader.’”
All the elders of Israel came to King David at Hebron, and the king made a deal with them before God. Then they anointed David and made him king over all of Israel.

David was thirty years old when he started his reign, and he ruled for forty years. He was king of Judah in Hebron for seven and a half years, and then he ruled all of Israel and Judah from Jerusalem for thirty-three years.

David and his crew immediately headed to Jerusalem to take on the Jebusites who lived there. But the Jebusites were cocky and said, “You can’t get in here! Even our blind and lame citizens could keep you out.” They seriously thought David had no chance.

But David went for it anyway and captured the fortress of Zion, which is now known as the City of David. That day, David said, “To beat these Jebusites, you gotta go for their water supply. And forget this ‘lame and blind’ crew that I’m so sick of.” He was so over it that it became a saying: “No lame and blind people allowed in the palace.”

David moved into the fortress and called it the “City of David.” He built up the city from the terraces inward. David just kept getting stronger and more successful because the God of Angel Armies was with him.

Around this time, Hiram, the king of Tyre, sent messengers to David with cedar logs. He also sent carpenters and stonemasons to build a palace for David. David saw this as a sign that God had officially made him king of Israel and was making his kingdom a big deal for the sake of his people, Israel.
After he left Hebron, David got more concubines and wives from Jerusalem, and had more sons and daughters. These are the names of the kids he had in Jerusalem:
Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.

When the Philistines heard that David had been made king over all of Israel, they came looking for him. David found out and went down to his stronghold. When the Philistines showed up, they spread out their troops in the Rephaim Valley.
Then David asked God, “Should I go fight the Philistines? Will you help me win?”
“Go for it,” God said. “I got you. I’ll help you beat them.”

So David went to a place called Baal Perazim and totally crushed them. Afterward, David said, “God just burst through my enemies like a flood of water.” That’s why he named the place Baal Perazim (which means “The Master Who Bursts Through”). The Philistines ran off and left their idols behind, so David and his soldiers picked them up.
Later, it was like a sequel. The Philistines came back and set up their troops in the Rephaim Valley again. David prayed to God again.

This time God said, “Don’t attack them from the front. Go around behind them and ambush them from the grove of sacred trees. When you hear a rustling sound in the trees, that’s your cue to move out. It means I’m going ahead of you to wreck the Philistine camp.”
David did exactly what God told him to do. He chased the Philistines all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.

title: God's Ark is WILD, David's Dance Moves are WILDER
paragraphs: So David got all of Israel's best troops together—like, thirty whole divisions of them. He and his soldiers went to Baalah to bring back the Ark of God. You know, the one that's called by the Name of God-of-the-Angel-Armies, who sits enthroned over the angels on the Ark itself.

They put the Ark of God on a brand-new oxcart and rolled it out of Abinadab's house on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, Abinadab's sons, were driving the new cart with the Ark. Ahio was out front, and Uzzah was right there next to the Ark. David and the whole crew from Israel were basically having a huge parade. They were singing like crazy and playing all sorts of instruments—mandolins, harps, tambourines, you name it. But when they got to Nacon's threshing floor, the oxen stumbled. Uzzah reached out and grabbed the Ark to steady it. And then, bam. God got super angry with Uzzah and struck him down right there because he'd disrespected the Ark. Uzzah died on the spot, right next to it. It was intense.

David was actually pretty ticked off that God had lashed out at Uzzah like that. They even named that place Perez Uzzah, which means 'The-Explosion-Against-Uzzah.' After that, David was genuinely afraid of God and was like, 'This Ark is way too intense. How am I ever gonna get it back to the City of David?' So he decided not to move the Ark any farther. Instead, he took it to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite. The Ark of God stayed at the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite for three months, and God totally blessed him and his entire household.

When King David heard that God had blessed Obed-Edom and his whole family because of the Ark, he was like, 'Okay, bet. I want in on that blessing.' So he went and brought the Ark of God up from Obed-Edom's house to the City of David, and this time it was a full-on party. They were making sacrifices of the best bulls all along the way. David, wearing a special priest's outfit, was dancing before God with all his might. The whole country was shouting and blasting trumpets as they brought the Ark in. But as the Ark of God entered the City of David, Saul's daughter Michal was watching from a window. When she saw King David jumping and dancing around for God, she was totally disgusted and looked down on him.

They brought the Ark of God in and set it up inside the tent David had prepared for it. David then worshiped God, offering up a bunch of sacrifices. After all the offerings were done, he blessed the people in the name of God-of-the-Angel-Armies. Then he gave everyone in the crowd, guys and girls, a loaf of bread, a date cake, and a raisin cake. After that, everyone went home.

David went home to bless his own family, but Michal, Saul's daughter, came out to meet him and said, 'Wow, the king of Israel really made a name for himself today—stripping down in front of the servant girls like some kind of street performer!' David shot back at Michal, 'I'll dance for God all I want! He picked me over your dad and your whole family and made me the leader of God's people, Israel. So yeah, I'll dance to honor God—and I'll get even crazier than this. And if I look like a fool, so be it. But those servant girls you're so worried about? They'll think it's awesome.'
And Michal, Saul's daughter, never had any children for the rest of her life.

title: God's Ultimate Glow-Up for David's Family
paragraphs: So, King David was finally chilling, living his best life. God had basically taken care of all his enemies, so it was all peace and quiet. Then one day, David says to Nathan the prophet, 'Yo, check this out. I'm living in this sick cedar palace, but God's Ark is just sitting in a regular old tent. Kinda weird, right?'
Nathan was like, 'Bro, whatever you're thinking, just go for it. God's got your back.'

But that same night, God hit Nathan up with a message. He was like, 'Go tell my boy David what's up. This is what I have to say about that: You think you're gonna build a 'house' for me to live in? Seriously? I haven't lived in a 'house' since I brought the Israelites out of Egypt. The whole time, I've just been on the move with a tent. And in all my travels with Israel, did I ever once say to any of the leaders I put in charge, 'Yo, why haven't you built me a cedar house?'

'So here's the deal, tell my servant David this: The God of the Angel Armies says: I literally picked you from a field where you were just following sheep and made you the leader of my people, Israel. I was with you everywhere you went and took down all your enemies for you. And now, I'm making you famous, like, A-list famous on earth. And I'm setting up a permanent spot for my people, Israel, and planting them there so they can have their own home and not get pushed around anymore. No more evil people messing with you like they used to, not even like in the old days when I had judges ruling over Israel. And finally, I'm giving you a break from all your enemies.'

'And on top of all that, God's got another message for you: God himself is gonna build YOU a house! When your life is over and you're buried with your ancestors, I'm gonna raise up your own kid—your actual flesh and blood—to take your place, and I'll make his kingdom solid. He's the one who will build a house for my name, and I'll make sure his kingdom lasts forever. I'll be a father to him, and he'll be a son to me. When he messes up, I'll discipline him like any dad would, with the normal struggles of life. But I'll never take my love away from him like I did with Saul, the guy before you that I for sure removed. Your family and your kingdom are set for life, permanently. I'm watching over them! And your throne will always be there, solid as a rock.'
So Nathan went and told David literally everything he saw and heard in that vision, word for word.

Then King David went in, sat down in front of God, and prayed this: 'Who am I, my Lord GOD, and what's my family, that you've brought me this far? But that's like, nothing compared to what's coming. You've talked about my family's future, like, way down the road, and gave me a sneak peek of tomorrow, my Lord GOD! What can I even say to all this? You know me, Lord GOD, for who I really am. You did all this not because of me, but because of who YOU are—straight from your heart!—and you let me in on the secret.'

'This is why you're so great, Lord GOD! There's no one like you, no other God but you. We've heard it with our own ears. And who's like your people, Israel? They're a one-of-a-kind nation that you, God, went out of your way to save for yourself (and got super famous for it), doing amazing and kinda scary things, kicking out nations and their gods left and right as you saved your people from Egypt. You made Israel your very own people, forever. And you, God, became their God.'

'So now, great God, this promise you've made to me and my family, please make it official, forever! Do exactly what you said! Then your name will be famous forever, and people will be like, 'The God of the Angel Armies is God over Israel!' And your servant David's family will be secure with you watching over them. Because you, God of the Angel Armies, God of Israel, told me straight up, 'I will build you a house.' That's what gave me the guts to even pray this prayer to you.'

'And now, Lord GOD, since you are who you are, and your words are always true, and you've just promised this amazing thing to me, please, just one more thing: Bless my family. Keep an eye on them always. You pretty much already said you would, Lord GOD! Oh, may your blessing be on my family forever!'

title: David's Unstoppable Winning Streak
paragraphs: So after that, David went after the Philistines and totally wrecked them. He basically took over their whole turf.

Then he took on Moab. Get this—he made them lie down on the ground, and then randomly executed two-thirds of them. SSuper harsh. He spared the other third,but they had to serve David and pay him taxes.

Next up, David was on his way to get his power back at the Euphrates River when he ran into Hadadezer son of Rehob, the king of Zobah. David's army crushed him, capturing 1,000 chariots, 7,000 horsemen, and 20,000 soldiers. He lamed most of the chariot horses but kept 100 for himself.

Then the Arameans from Damascus tried to help out Hadadezer, king of Zobah, but that was a bad move. David's crew took down 22,000 of them. David basically set up his own guys to rule in Damascus, and the Arameans had to pay up too. God kept giving David victory everywhere he went.
David also snagged all the gold shields from Hadadezer's officials and brought them to Jerusalem. Plus, he looted a ton of bronze from Hadadezer's cities, Tebah and Berothai.

When Toi, the king of Hamath, heard that David had completely owned Hadadezer's army, he sent his son Joram to congratulate David. Toi and Hadadezer were enemies, so he was pretty stoked. Joram brought gifts of silver, gold, and bronze. King David dedicated all this stuff to God, along with the silver and gold he'd taken from all the other nations he conquered—Aram, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, Amalek, aand all the loot from Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
David even built a monument to celebrate his victory when he got back from beating the Arameans.
Abishai, son of Zeruiah, also had a huge win against the Edomites in the Salt Valley, taking out 18,000 of them. David set up his own government in Edom, and the Edomites became his subjects too.
God gave David victory wherever he went.
So David ruled over all of Israel, and he was a solid ruler—fair and just to everyone.
Here's who was on his squad:
Joab son of Zeruiah was the general of the army;
Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the royal historian;
Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were the priests;
Seraiah was the secretary;
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was in charge of the Kerethites and Pelethites (basically the royal bodyguards);
And David’s sons were priests.

title: From Zero to Hero: A King's Promise
paragraphs: So one day, David was like, “Yo, is anyone from Saul’s family still around? I wanna do something really kind for them, to honor my boy Jonathan.”
Turns out, a guy named Ziba who used to work for Saul was right there. So they brought him to David. The king asked, “You Ziba?”
And he was like, “Yup, that’s me.”
The king asked, “So for real, is there anyone left from Saul’s family? I need to show them some major kindness, like the kind God shows.”
Ziba said, “Well, yeah, Jonathan’s son is still alive. He can’t walk well, though, he’s lame in both feet.”
“Where is he at?”
“He’s crashing at this guy Makir son of Ammiel’s place in Lo Debar.”
King David didn’t waste any time. He immediately sent his guys to go get him from the house of Makir son of Ammiel in Lo Debar.
So when Mephibosheth, Jonathan’s son (and Saul’s grandson), showed up, he bowed down super low to show David respect.
David just said his name, “Mephibosheth.”
“Yeah? That’s me.”

“Hey, don’t be scared,” David said. “I’m about to do something awesome for you because of your dad, Jonathan. First off, I’m giving you back all the land that belonged to your grandpa Saul. On top of that, from now on, you’re gonna eat with me at my table.”
Mephibosheth was shook. He could barely look at the king and was like, “Who am I even? Why are you being so nice to a nobody like me?”

Then David called over Ziba, Saul’s old main guy, and told him, “Everything that used to be Saul’s and his family’s, I’ve just given to your master’s grandson. You, your sons, and your workers are gonna farm his land and bring in the crops to provide for him. But Mephibosheth himself, your master’s grandson, will always eat at my table.” Btw, Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
Ziba was like, “Whatever my lord the king commands, I’ll do it.”

And just like that, Mephibosheth started eating at David’s table, like he was one of the king’s own sons. Mephibosheth also had a young son named Mica. And everyone in Ziba’s house started working for Mephibosheth.
Mephibosheth ended up living in Jerusalem and always ate at the king’s table. And yeah, he was lame in both feet.

title: When Showing Kindness Goes Horribly Wrong
paragraphs: So, a while later, the king of the Ammonites died, and his son Hanun took over the throne. David was like, 'Yo, I should show some love to Hanun, son of Nahash. His dad was always cool with me, so I wanna be cool with him.' So, David sent some guys to give Hanun his condolences for his dad's passing.

But when David's crew arrived in the Ammonite territory, the Ammonite leaders pulled Hanun aside and were like, 'Bro, are you for real? You actually think David is honoring your dad by sending these guys? Nah, he's totally just sending spies to scope out the city and figure out how to attack it.'
So Hanun actually listened to them. He grabbed David's guys, shaved off half of each of their beards, chopped their robes in half so their butts were hanging out, and then sent them home. Wild.

When David heard what happened, he was like, 'No way.' He sent someone to meet his guys because they were beyond embarrassed. The king told them, 'Just chill in Jericho until your beards grow back. Don't come back to the capital until then.'

When the Ammonites realized they had seriously messed up and David was mad, they basically panicked. They hired a bunch of mercenaries: twenty thousand Aramean soldiers from Beth-Rehob and Zobah, a thousand guys from the king of Maacah, and twelve thousand from Tob.
When David got the news, he sent out Joab with his whole squad of elite fighters.

The Ammonites came out and got into battle formation at their city gate. The Aramean mercs from Zobah, Rehob, Tob, and Maacah set up in the open fields. When Joab saw he was getting attacked from the front and the back, he picked his best soldiers and set them up to fight the Arameans. He put his brother Abishai in charge of the rest of the army to take on the Ammonites. Then he said, 'If the Arameans are too strong for me, you gotta come help me. And if the Ammonites are too much for you, I'll come help you. Be brave! We're fighting for our people and for God's cities. God's gonna do what he thinks is right.'

But as soon as Joab and his soldiers moved in to attack the Arameans, the mercs just turned and ran. It was a total retreat. Then the Ammonites, seeing their hired help bail, also ran away from Abishai and hid back in their city.
So Joab stopped the attack on the Ammonites and went back to Jerusalem.

When the Arameans saw how badly Israel had beaten them, they regrouped. Hadadezer sent for more Aramean troops from across the Euphrates River, and they all gathered at Helam, led by Shobach, Hadadezer's top general. David heard about all this.

So David gathered all of Israel, crossed the Jordan River, and went to Helam. The Arameans got ready to fight David, and the battle was on. But once again, the Arameans scattered in front of Israel. David's army took out seven hundred chariot drivers and forty thousand cavalry. They also fatally wounded Shobach, the enemy commander, who died right there on the battlefield. When all the kings who were allied with Hadadezer saw they got wrecked by Israel, they made a peace treaty and became Israel's subjects. After that, the Arameans were too scared to ever help the Ammonites again.

title: King's Secret Scandal & a Soldier's Fate
paragraphs: So, when spring rolled around again, the same time the Ammonites had first started beef, David sent Joab and the whole Israelite army to finish them off for good. They surrounded the city of Rabbah, but David just chilled in Jerusalem.

One afternoon, David woke up from a nap and was taking a walk on his palace roof. From up there, he saw this woman bathing, and she was drop-dead gorgeous. David sent someone to ask who she was, and they were like, 'Isn't that Bathsheba, Eliam's daughter and the wife of Uriah the Hittite?' So David sent his guys to bring her to him. When she got there, he slept with her. (This was during her 'purification' time after her period, btw.) Then she went back home. Not long after, she figured out she was pregnant.
Later she sent a message to David: 'I'm pregnant.'
David hit up Joab and was like, 'Send Uriah the Hittite to me.' So Joab sent him.
When Uriah showed up, David asked him how everything was going at the warfront—how Joab and the troops were doing. Then he told Uriah, 'Go home, take a shower, and get some rest.'
After Uriah left, the king sent a spy after him. But Uriah didn't even go home. He just crashed at the palace entrance with the king's guards.
Someone told David that Uriah hadn't gone home. He asked him, 'Dude, you just got back from a long trip. Why didn't you go home?'

Uriah told David, 'The Ark of the Covenant is out there in a tent with the armies of Israel and Judah. My commander Joab and his officers are sleeping in the open fields. So how could I go home, eat and drink, and hook up with my wife? I swear on your life, I won't do it!'
'Alright then,' David said, 'do what you want. Stay here today, and I'll send you back tomorrow.' So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem for the day.
The next day, David invited him over, got him wasted, but that night Uriah still went and slept with the king's servants. He didn't go home.
In the morning, David wrote a letter to Joab and had Uriah deliver it. The letter said, 'Put Uriah on the front lines where the fighting is craziest. Then, pull back and leave him there to die.'

So Joab, who was in the middle of the siege, put Uriah in a spot where he knew the enemy's best fighters were. When the city's soldiers came out to fight, some of David's men were killed, and Uriah the Hittite was one of them.

Joab sent a full report of the battle to David. He told the messenger, 'After you tell the king everything that happened, if he gets mad, just add, 'Oh, and by the way, your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead.''

Joab's messenger got to Jerusalem and gave the king the full story. He said, 'The enemy was stronger than us. They came at us in the open, and we had to push them back to the city gate. But then they started shooting arrows at us from the city wall, and eighteen of the king's soldiers died.'

When the messenger finished his report, David got pissed at Joab. He took it out on the messenger: 'Why did you get so close to the city? Didn't you know they'd shoot at you from the wall? Don't you remember how Abimelech son of Jerub-Besheth died? Wasn't it a woman who dropped a millstone on him from the wall and killed him at Thebez? Why would you go so close to the wall!'
'Oh, and by the way,' the messenger added, 'your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead.'

When the messenger finished his report, David was actually furious at Joab, and he vented it on the messenger: 'Why did you get so close to the city? Didn't you know they'd attack you from the wall? Don't you remember how Abimelech son of Jerub-Besheth died? A woman dropped a millstone on him from the wall and crushed him at Thebez! Why did you go so close to the wall?!' "By the way," the messenger added, "your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead." Then David told the messenger, 'Oh, I see. Tell Joab, 'Don't sweat it. People die in war—you never know who's next. Just attack the city even harder and destroy it.' Go encourage Joab.'
When Uriah's wife heard her husband was dead, she mourned for him. After the mourning period was over, David sent for her and she came to his house. She became his wife and they had a son.

title: David's BIG Mistake & The Consequences
paragraphs: God was really not happy with what David did, so He sent Nathan to talk to him. Nathan said, “Okay, picture this: two guys in a city. One’s rich, one’s poor. The rich guy has tons of sheep and cows. The poor guy has just one little lamb he bought and raised. It grew up with him and his kids, like a pet. It ate his food, drank from his cup, slept in his bed. Basically, she was like a daughter to him.
“So one day, a visitor drops by the rich guy’s place. But the rich guy is too stingy to cook one of his own sheep. So he steals the poor man’s only lamb and serves it to his guest.”
David totally lost it. “As God lives,” he said to Nathan, “that guy should be cancelled! He has to pay back for the lamb four times over for being so cruel and cheap!”

Nathan just said, “You’re the man.” And then he dropped this message from God: “I’m the one who made you king. I saved you from Saul. I gave you his family, his wives, the whole kingdom. If that wasn’t enough, I would’ve given you more. So why did you disrespect me and do this evil thing? You murdered Uriah the Hittite with an Ammonite sword and then took his wife. Because you did that, your family will never be free from violence. I’m going to bring disaster on you from your own family. I’ll take your wives right in front of you and give them to your neighbor, and he’ll be with them in broad daylight. You did your thing in secret, but I’m going to do this in front of everyone.”
David confessed to Nathan, “I’ve sinned against God.”
Nathan replied, “Okay, but God has forgiven you. You won’t die. But because you gave God’s enemies a reason to mock him, the son born to you will die.”

After Nathan left, the child Uriah’s wife had with David got super sick. David begged God for the boy. He fasted, stayed in all night, and slept on the floor. His senior staff tried to get him up, but he wouldn’t. And he wouldn’t eat anything. On the seventh day, the child died. David’s servants were scared to tell him. They were like, “He wouldn’t listen to us when the kid was alive, what’s he gonna do now that he’s dead?”
But David saw them whispering and knew the boy had died.
He asked, “Is the boy dead?”
“Yes,” they said. “He’s dead.”
David got up, washed, changed his clothes, and went to worship God. Then he went home and asked for food. They gave it to him, and he ate.
His servants were confused. “What’s going on? You fasted and cried when the child was alive, but now that he’s dead, you’re up and eating.”

He said, “When he was alive, I fasted and cried, hoping God might be merciful and let him live. But now that he’s dead, why fast? I can’t bring him back. I’ll go to him one day, but he can’t come back to me.”

Then David went to comfort his wife, Bathsheba. They had another son and named him Solomon. God loved him and sent a message through Nathan the prophet to name him Jedidiah, which means “Beloved of God.”

Meanwhile, Joab was fighting the Ammonites and had captured the royal city’s water supply. He sent a message to David: “I’ve taken the water supply. You need to bring the rest of the army and finish the job, or I’ll capture the city and it’ll be named after me.” So David gathered the army, went to Rabbah, and captured it. He took the king’s crown, which was super heavy with gold and had a precious gem in it, and put it on his own head. They also took a massive amount of loot from the city.

David then took all the people from the city and forced them into slave labor with saws, picks, and axes, and made them work at brickyards. He did this to all the Ammonite cities. Then he and his army went back to Jerusalem.

title: The Royal Family's Darkest Secret
paragraphs: So, a while later, this terrible thing happened. King David's son, Absalom, had this super pretty sister named Tamar. And get this, their half-brother, Amnon, was totally obsessed with her. Like, he was making himself sick over it. Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon was stressing because he had no idea how to get with her. He had this one friend, Jonadab—the son of David's brother Shimeah—who was super street-smart. Jonadab was like, 'Bro, you're the king's son. Why are you so down bad every single day? Just tell me what's up.' "In a word, Tamar," Amnon said. "My brother Absalom's sister. I'm in love with her."
'It's Tamar,' Amnon said. 'Absalom's sister. I'm completely in love with her.'

'Okay, here's the plan,' said Jonadab. 'Go to your room and act like you're super sick. When your dad, the king, comes to check on you, just be like, "Hey Dad, can you ask my sister Tamar to come over and make me some food? I want to watch her make it and have her feed it to me."

So Amnon did it. He got in bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came by, Amnon said, 'Could you do me a solid? Ask Tamar to come make some of her famous dumplings for me right here, so I can watch and she can feed me.'
So David sent a message to Tamar, who was just chilling at home: 'Go over to your brother Amnon's place and make him some food.'

Tamar went to Amnon's house. She got out the dough, kneaded it, made the dumplings, and cooked them, all while he was watching from his bed. But when she brought the pot over and served him, he refused to eat.

Amnon was like, 'Everyone, get out of the house.' So they all left. Then he said to Tamar, 'Bring the food into my bedroom so we can eat in private.' So she took the dumplings she had made and brought them into his bedroom. But when she went to feed him, he grabbed her and said, 'Come to bed with me, sis.'

'No, brother!' she yelled. 'Don't do this to me! This is not okay in Israel! Don't do this horrible thing! I'll be so ashamed, I won't be able to show my face anywhere. And you—you'll be a total disgrace. Seriously, just talk to the king! He'll let you marry me.'
But he wouldn't listen. He was way stronger than her, so he raped her.
As soon as Amnon had raped her, he hated her. Like, an insane amount of hatred. The hate he felt for her was even stronger than the love he'd had before. 'Get up,' he said, 'and get out!'
'No, brother, please!' she said. 'Sending me away now is even worse than what you just did!'
But he still wouldn't listen. He called his servant and said, 'Get this woman out of here. Get her out of my sight and lock the door behind her.' So the servant threw her out and locked the door.

She was wearing a fancy dress with long sleeves, which was what virgin princesses wore back then. Tamar put ashes on her head, ripped her dress, put her head in her hands, and just walked away, sobbing like crazy.

Her brother Absalom saw her and was like, 'Did your brother Amnon just do something to you? Okay, listen, my dear sister, let's just keep this quiet for now. It's a family thing. He's still your brother. Don't let this destroy you.' So Tamar went to live in Absalom's house, feeling bitter and completely alone.

When King David heard the whole story, he was furious, but he didn't do anything to punish Amnon. David had a major soft spot for him because he was his firstborn son. Absalom, on the other hand, completely stopped talking to Amnon—not a single word, good or bad—because he hated him for what he did to his sister Tamar.

Two years passed. One day, Absalom was throwing a sheep-shearing party in Baal Hazor near Ephraim and invited all the king's sons. He also went to the king to invite him. 'Hey, I'm having a party. You should come, and bring your crew.'
But the king said, 'Nah, son. Not this time. It's too much trouble for you.' Absalom kept pushing, but David wouldn't go. He did give him his blessing, though.
Then Absalom said, 'Well, if you're not coming, can my brother Amnon at least come?'
'Why should he go with you?' the king asked. But Absalom was so persistent that the king finally gave in and let Amnon and all his other sons go.

Absalom threw a huge feast, fit for a king. Then he told his servants, 'Alright, listen up. When Amnon is drunk and feeling good, and I give you the signal, 'Get Amnon,' you kill him. Don't be scared—I'm the one giving the order. Be brave. You got this.'

Absalom's servants did exactly what he told them to do to Amnon. All the other brothers freaked out, jumped on their mules, and got out of there as fast as they could. While they were still on their way back, a rumor reached the king: 'Absalom just killed all of your sons—not a single one is left!' The king stood up, ripped his clothes, and threw himself on the ground. All his servants who were there did the same thing.

But then Jonadab, the son of David's brother Shimeah, showed up and said, 'My king, don't believe that all your sons are dead. Only Amnon is dead. This was Absalom's revenge plan ever since Amnon violated his sister Tamar. So don't make it worse by thinking all your sons are gone. It's just Amnon.'

Absalom fled. Just then the sentry on duty looked up and saw a cloud of dust on the Horonaim road, alongside the mountain. He went and told the king, 'I just saw a bunch of men on the Horonaim road, coming around the mountain.'
Just then, the guard on duty looked up and saw a bunch of people coming down the road by the mountain. He ran and told the king, 'I see a group of men on the road, coming around the mountain.'

Then Jonadab yelled to the king, 'See! It's your sons! They're coming, just like I said!' He barely got the words out before the king's sons burst in, crying and wailing. The king started crying too, along with all his servants. It was a total sob fest. David mourned for his son for a long, long time.

After Absalom ran away, he went to stay with Talmai son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur. He was there for three years. Eventually, the king stopped trying to get revenge on Absalom. He had finally accepted that Amnon was dead.

title: Setting a Field on Fire to See the King?!
paragraphs: So, Joab, this guy Zeruiah's son, totally knew the king was still torn up about Absalom. He sent for this super wise woman from a town called Tekoa and was like, “Okay, here’s the plan. You’re gonna pretend you’re in major mourning. Wear all black, don’t even brush your hair, make it look like you’ve been grieving for ages. Then go to the king and say this…” And Joab gave her the whole script.
The woman from Tekoa went to the king, did a super deep bow, and said, “Your Majesty, you gotta help me!”
He was like, “What’s up? How can I help?”

She said, “I’m a widow. My husband’s dead. I had two sons, and they got into this huge fight out in a field. There was nobody around to break it up, and one of them hit the other and killed him. Now the whole family is ganging up on me, demanding, ‘Hand over the murderer so we can kill him for killing his brother!’ They’re trying to get rid of the only heir I have left and basically snuff out my last little bit of hope. If they do that, there’ll be nothing left of my husband—not even his name—on this whole planet.

“So, I got brave and decided to come to you, my king. They’re making my life a nightmare, and I’m scared. I told myself, ‘I’ll just go to the king. Maybe he’ll actually do something!’ I figured when the king hears my story, he’ll step in and save me from this guy who wants to get rid of both me and my son, and our part of God’s inheritance—everything! As your servant, I was just hoping that whatever you say will be the final word, because you’re like an angel from God, you can tell what’s good and what’s evil. Hope God is with you!”
The king said, "Go home. I'll take care of this for you."
“I’ll take full responsibility for whatever happens,” the woman of Tekoa said. “I don’t want you or your reputation to get messed up because of this.”
“Bring me the guy who’s been giving you a hard time,” the king said. “I’ll make sure he never bothers you again.”
“Please, can you swear by God’s name,” the woman said, “so this dude who thinks he’s the law doesn’t just destroy everything, not to mention kill my son?”
“As surely as God is real,” he said, “not a single hair on your son’s head will be touched. I promise.”
Then she asked, “Can I just say one more thing, my king?”
He said, “Go for it.”

“Well,” the woman said, “why have you basically done the same thing to God’s people? By making this decision, you’re kind of calling yourself out, since you won’t bring your own exiled son back home. Look, we all die eventually. It’s like spilling water on the ground—you can’t get it back. But God doesn’t just take a life. He figures out ways to bring back the person who was kicked out.”
The king then said, “I’m gonna ask you a question. And I want a straight answer.”
“Of course,” she said. “Whatever you want to ask, my king.”
The king said, “Is Joab in on this? Did he put you up to this?”

“On your life, my king, you can’t get anything past the king! Yes, it was your servant Joab. He gave me this whole idea and told me exactly what to say. He did it because he wanted to change things up. But you, my king, are as wise as one of God’s angels, you know everything that’s going on in the world.”
The king said to Joab, “Fine, I’ll do it. Go and bring the young man Absalom back.”
Joab bowed down super low and thanked the king. “Now I know for sure that you still trust me and I’m in your good graces, since you’re actually taking my advice.”

Joab got up, went to Geshur, and brought Absalom back to Jerusalem. But the king said, “He can go back to his own house, but he is not allowed to see my face.” So Absalom went home but wasn’t allowed to see the king.

And this Absalom guy! Seriously, there wasn’t a single dude in all of Israel who was as famous for being handsome. He was flawless from head to toe! When he cut his hair—which he did every spring because it got so heavy—the hair from his head weighed over two pounds! Absalom had three sons and one daughter. Her name was Tamar, and she was a total beauty.

Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two whole years and never once saw the king face-to-face. He sent for Joab to try and get a meeting with the king, but Joab wouldn’t come. He tried a second time, and Joab still ghosted him. So he told his servants, “Listen up. Joab’s field is right next to mine, and he’s got barley growing in it. Go set it on fire.” So Absalom’s servants torched the field. That finally got Joab’s attention. He went to Absalom’s house and said, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?!”

Absalom answered, “Look, I sent for you, I told you to come quick. I wanted to send you to the king to ask, ‘What was the point of me even coming back from Geshur? I would’ve been better off staying there!’ Just let me see the king. If he thinks I’m guilty of something, then fine, he can kill me.”
Joab went to the king and told him everything. Absalom was then called in. He came and bowed down super respectfully in front of him. And the king kissed Absalom.

title: My Son is Trying to Steal My Kingdom?!
paragraphs: So after a while, Absalom started acting like a total big shot. He got himself a fancy chariot and had fifty guys running ahead of him, like some kind of VIP. He'd wake up super early every morning and post up by the road at the city gate. Whenever someone came to the king with a problem, Absalom would call them over and be like, 'Yo, where you from?'
And the person would say, 'I'm from one of the tribes of Israel.'

Then Absalom would hit them with, 'Look, you've got a really strong case, but let's be real, the king isn't going to listen to you.' Then he'd say, 'For real, why doesn't someone just make me a judge? Anyone with an issue could come to me and I'd make sure things were fair.' And whenever someone tried to bow to him or show him a lot of respect, he'd just brush it off and treat them like an equal, which made them feel super important. Absalom did this with everyone who came to see the king, and he totally won over the hearts of all the people in Israel.

After four years of this, Absalom went to the king and said, 'Hey, can I go to Hebron? I need to fulfill a promise I made to God. When I was living in Geshur, I promised that if God brought me back to Jerusalem, I'd dedicate my life to serving him.'
The king said, 'Go for it, you have my blessing.' So Absalom got up and left for Hebron.

But then, Absalom sent secret agents to all the tribes of Israel with a message: 'When you hear the sound of the ram's horn, that's the signal. You need to shout, 'Absalom is the king in Hebron!'' About two hundred men went with Absalom from Jerusalem, but they were completely clueless. They were just invited to a thing and had no idea they were part of a plot. While Absalom was offering sacrifices, he also got Ahithophel the Gilonite, one of David's own advisors, to join him. He called him from his hometown, Giloh. The conspiracy got super strong, and more and more people started supporting Absalom.
Then, someone came to David and told him, 'The whole country is siding with Absalom!'
David immediately told all his servants in Jerusalem, 'We gotta go, now! We have to run for our lives, or Absalom will get us. Hurry, he's about to tear this city down and kill us all!'
The king's servants were like, 'Whatever you say, boss. We're with you all the way.'

So the king and his whole family escaped on foot. He left ten of his concubines behind to take care of the palace. They left, walking step by step, and paused at the very last house as the entire army marched past him—all the Kerethites, Pelethites, and the six hundred Gittites who had come with him from Gath.

The king called out to Ittai the Gittite, 'What are you doing here? You should go back and be with King Absalom. You're a foreigner here, and you just got kicked out of your own country. You only got here yesterday, so why should I make you wander around with us while I'm basically homeless? Go back, and take your family with you. May God's grace and truth be with you!'
But Ittai answered, 'As God is my witness, and as you are my king, wherever you go, I'll go. Whether it means life or death, I'm with you.'
'Alright then,' David said, 'let's go.' And so they continued on, Ittai the Gittite with all his men and their families.

The whole country was crying loudly as everyone passed by. The king crossed the Kidron Brook, and the army headed toward the wilderness. Zadok the priest was there too, with the Levites, carrying the Ark of the Covenant of God. They set the Ark of God down, and Abiathar stood by it until everyone had left the city.

Then the king told Zadok, 'Take the Ark back to the city. If I'm still in God's good graces, he'll bring me back and let me see it again. But if he says, 'I'm not happy with you,' then fine. He can do whatever he wants with me.'

The king told Zadok the priest, 'Here's the plan: go back to the city peacefully. Take your son Ahimaaz and Jonathan, Abiathar's son, with you. I'll wait at a spot in the wilderness across the river until I hear from you about what's going on.' So Zadok and Abiathar took the Ark of God back to Jerusalem and left it there. Meanwhile, David went up the Mount of Olives, crying. He covered his head and walked barefoot, and his whole army was with him, their heads covered, weeping as they went up the mountain.
Then someone told David, 'Ahithophel has joined Absalom's conspiracy.' David prayed, 'Oh, God, please make Ahithophel's advice sound like foolishness.'

When David got to the top of the hill where people worshiped God, Hushai the Arkite was there waiting for him. His clothes were torn, and he had dirt on his head. David told him, 'If you come with me, you'll just be more baggage. You should go back to the city and say to Absalom, 'I'm your servant now, O King. I used to serve your father, but now I serve you.' If you do that, you can mess up Ahithophel's advice for me. The priests Zadok and Abiathar are already there. Whatever you hear in the palace, tell them. Their two sons, Ahimaaz and Jonathan, are with them. You can send any information you get to me through them.'
So Hushai, David's friend, went into Jerusalem, arriving at the exact same time as Absalom.

title: David Gets Cursed Out & Absalom's Savage Move
paragraphs: So, right after David made it over the top of the hill, this dude Ziba, who was Mephibosheth's manager, rolled up to meet him. He had a whole crew of donkeys loaded with a hundred loaves of bread, a hundred raisin cakes, a hundred baskets of fresh fruit, and a big ol' skin of wine.
The king was like, "Yo, what's all this?"
Ziba explained, "The donkeys are for your family to ride, the bread and fruit are for your squad to eat, and the wine is for anyone who's totally exhausted from the wilderness."
The king then asked, "And where's your master's grandson?"
Ziba said, "He's back in Jerusalem. He was basically like, 'Today's the day Israel is gonna give me back my grandpa's kingdom.'"
The king declared, "Aight, bet. Everything that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours."
Ziba was like, "Wow, how can I even thank you? I'm forever in your debt, my king; I hope you always see me this way!"

When the king got to Bahurim, this guy from Saul's extended family just appeared. His name was Shimei, son of Gera. He started following David and his crew, just yelling insults and throwing rocks at David and all his soldiers and servants. While cursing them out, he screamed, "Get outta here, you murderer, you psycho! God's giving you payback for all the messed up stuff you did to Saul's family and for stealing his kingdom. God handed the kingdom over to your son Absalom. Look at you now—you're ruined! Good riddance, you pathetic old man!"
Abishai, son of Zeruiah, was like, "This trash dog can't be dissing my king like that—let me go over there and chop his head off!"
But the king said, "Why are you sons of Zeruiah always jumping in and making things complicated? If he's cursing me, it's because God told him to, like, 'Curse David.' So who are you to question it?"

David went on, talking to Abishai and his other servants, "Look, my own son, my actual flesh and blood, is trying to kill me right now. Compared to that, this Benjaminite is small potatoes. Just leave him alone; let him curse. It's like he's preaching God's word to me. And who knows, maybe God will see the mess I'm in today and flip these curses into something good."
So David and his men kept walking down the road, and Shimei just kept following them along the hill, cursing, throwing stones at them, and kicking up dust.
By the time they got to the Jordan River, David and his whole crew were completely wiped. They stopped there to rest and get their energy back.
Meanwhile, Absalom and all his guys were now in Jerusalem.
And Ahithophel was with them.
Then Hushai the Arkite, David's friend, showed up and greeted Absalom, saying, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"
Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this how you treat your good friend? Why didn't you go with your boy David?"

Hushai replied, "Because I'm with the guy that God, this nation, and all of Israel have picked. And I'm staying with him. Besides, who else is there to serve but the son? Just like I served your dad, I'm ready to serve you now."
Then Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, "You got any advice? What's our next move?"

Ahithophel told Absalom, "Go sleep with your father's concubines, the ones he left behind to take care of the palace. Everyone will hear that you've publicly disrespected your father, and it'll boost the morale of everyone on your team." So Absalom set up a tent on the palace roof where everyone could see, and he went in and slept with his father's concubines.
Back in those days, any advice Ahithophel gave was treated like it came straight from God. That's how much people respected his advice, both when he was with David and now with Absalom.

title: The Ultimate Escape Plan vs. A Fatal Mistake
paragraphs: Then Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Yo, let me pick 12,000 dudes and go after David tonight. I'll catch him when he's exhausted and totally off-guard. His whole crew will scatter, and I'll just take out David. Then I'll bring the army back to you like a bride returning to her husband. You're only after one guy, after all. Then everyone can just chill."
Absalom thought it was an amazing plan, and all the elders of Israel were on board.
But then Absalom was like, "Hold up, get Hushai the Arkite in here. Let's see what he has to say."
So Hushai came in, and Absalom laid it out for him: "Ahithophel gave us this plan. Should we do it? What's your take?"

Hushai said, "Honestly, the advice Ahithophel gave this time is not it. You know your dad and his men are total beasts, and they're furious—like a mama bear who got her cubs stolen. Plus, your dad is a master strategist; he's definitely not just sleeping around at a time like this. For all we know, he's probably hiding out in a cave or something right now. If he jumps your guys from an ambush, the word will spread like wildfire: 'Absalom's army is getting wrecked!' Even your bravest soldiers with hearts of lions will fall apart at that news, because everyone in Israel knows your father is a legendary fighter, and so are the men with him.

"Here's what I think you should do: Gather the whole country, from Dan to Beersheba, an army as massive as the sand on the seashore, and you lead them personally. We'll smoke him out wherever he is, dropping on him like dew on the ground, and trust me, not a single person will be left standing. If he's hiding in a city, the whole army will bring ropes to that city and literally drag it into a ravine—not even a pebble will be left!"
Absalom and all his guys agreed that Hushai the Arkite's plan was way better than Ahithophel's. (It was actually God's plan to wreck Ahithophel's good advice to bring Absalom down.)

Then Hushai went to the priests Zadok and Abiathar and told them, "Ahithophel advised Absalom and the elders this, but I advised them that. Now, you gotta send a message to David ASAP: 'Don't stay the night on this side of the river; cross it immediately, or the king and everyone with him will be completely wiped out.'"

Jonathan and Ahimaaz were waiting at En Rogel. A servant girl would come and give them messages, and then they'd go tell King David, because it was too risky for them to be seen in the city. But a soldier saw them and told Absalom, so the two of them got out of there fast and went to a man's house in Bahurim. He had a well in his yard, and they climbed down into it. The man's wife took a rug, covered the well, and spread grain over it so it looked totally normal. Soon, Absalom's servants came to the house and asked the woman, "Have you seen Ahimaaz and Jonathan?"
The woman said, "They were heading toward the river."
They searched but couldn't find them, so they went back to Jerusalem.
Once the coast was clear, Ahimaaz and Jonathan climbed out of the well and went to report to King David: "Get up and cross the river now! Ahithophel has a plan against you!"
David and his whole crew got up and immediately started crossing the Jordan. By sunrise, every single person had made it across.

When Ahithophel saw that his advice wasn't followed, he saddled his donkey and went back to his hometown. After writing his will and getting his affairs in order, he hanged himself and died. He was buried in his family's tomb.

Around the time David got to Mahanaim, Absalom crossed the Jordan with the entire army of Israel. Absalom had put Amasa in charge of the army, replacing Joab. (Amasa was the son of a guy named Ithra, an Ishmaelite who had married Abigail, who was the daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mom.) Israel and Absalom set up camp in Gilead.

When David arrived at Mahanaim, Shobi son of Nahash from Ammonite Rabbah, Makir son of Ammiel from Lo Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim brought a bunch of stuff: beds, blankets, bowls, and jugs full of wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, and lentils, plus honey, curds, and cheese. They gave all this to David and his army to eat, because they said, "The army must be starving, exhausted, and thirsty out here in the wilderness."

title: The Tragic End of Absalom & A Father's Heartbreak
paragraphs: So David got his squad ready. He set up captains for groups of a thousand and a hundred. Then he sent them out: one-third of the army was with Joab, one-third with Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and the last third with Ittai the Gittite.
Then the king was like, “I’m rolling out with you guys.”

But his men were like, “Nah, you can’t come. If we have to fall back, the enemy won’t even care. If half of us die, it’s whatever to them. But you? You’re worth ten thousand of us. It’s way better if you stay in the city and support us from there.”
“Aight, bet,” said the king. “I’ll do what you guys think is best.” So he stood by the city gate as the whole army marched out, crew by crew.
Then the king gave orders to Joab, Abishai, and Ittai: “Hey, for my sake, be gentle with the young man Absalom.” The whole army heard what the king commanded the three captains about Absalom.

The army went out to face Israel, and the battle went down in the Forest of Ephraim. It was a total disaster for Israel’s army that day; David’s crew won big time. It was a crazy slaughter—twenty thousand men died! The fighting was chaotic and all over the place. The forest itself ended up taking more lives than the actual fighting!

Absalom, riding his mule, randomly ran into David’s men. As he was trying to get away, the mule went under this massive oak tree, and Absalom’s head got tangled in the branches. He was left just dangling there between the sky and the ground, while the mule just kept on running.
A soldier saw the whole thing and went to tell Joab, “Yo, I just saw Absalom hanging from an oak tree!”
Joab said to the guy, “You saw him? Why didn’t you just take him out right there? I would’ve given you ten pieces of silver and a sick belt.”

The soldier replied to Joab, "Bro, even for a thousand pieces of silver, I wouldn’t touch the king’s son. We all heard the king tell you, Abishai, and Ittai, ‘Protect the young man Absalom for me.’ I’d be risking my life, ‘cause the king finds out everything. And you? You would’ve just stood there and let me take the fall!”

Joab was like, “I don’t have time for this.” He grabbed three daggers and stabbed Absalom right in the heart while he was still alive in the tree. By then, ten of Joab’s armor-bearers had surrounded Absalom; they finished him off.
Then Joab blew the trumpet to signal the army to stop chasing the Israelites. They took Absalom’s body, threw it into a huge pit in the forest, and piled a massive stack of rocks over it.
Meanwhile, Israel’s entire army bailed, every man for himself, heading home.

When Absalom was alive, he had built a pillar for himself in the King’s Valley. He was like, “I don’t have a son to carry on my name,” so he named the pillar after himself. To this day, it’s called “The Absalom Memorial.”

Ahimaaz, Zadok’s son, said, “Let me run and tell the king the good news that God has saved him from his enemies.” But Joab told him, “You’re not the one bringing good news today. Maybe some other day, but today is not a ‘good news’ day.” (He said this because the king’s son was dead.)
Then Joab ordered a Cushite man, “You go. Tell the king what you saw.”
“Yessir,” the Cushite said, and took off running.
But Ahimaaz, son of Zadok, wouldn’t give up. He begged Joab, “Who cares? Let me run too, right after the Cushite.”
Joab was like, “Why are you so obsessed with running? You’re not gonna get any props for this, I promise you.”
“I don’t care; let me run.”
“Fine,” said Joab, “run.” So Ahimaaz took a shortcut through the valley and actually passed the Cushite.

David was sitting between the two city gates. The watchman on the wall went up to the roof, looked out, and saw a single runner. The watchman shouted down to the king. The king said, “If he’s alone, it’s gotta be good news!”
As the runner got closer, the watchman saw another runner and yelled down to the gatekeeper, “Look, another guy running by himself.”
The king said, “This has to be good news, too.”
Then the watchman said, “I can see the first guy now; he runs like Ahimaaz, son of Zadok.”
“He’s a good dude,” said the king. “He’s definitely bringing good news.”
Ahimaaz called out to the king, “All good!” Then he bowed down with his face to the ground. “Shoutout to your God; He handed over the guys who rebelled against you, my king.”
The king asked, “But what about the young man Absalom? Is he okay?”
Ahimaaz said, “I saw a huge commotion right when Joab was sending me off, but I have no idea what it was about.”
The king told him, “Step aside and wait over there.” So he did.
Then the Cushite arrived and said, “Good news, my king! God gave you the victory today over everyone who rebelled against you!”
“But,” the king asked, “is the young man Absalom okay?”
The Cushite answered, “I wish all the enemies of my king, and everyone who tries to harm you, would end up just like that young man.”
The king was completely shattered. Heartbroken, he went up to the room above the gate and just wept. As he cried, he kept saying,
“Oh, my son Absalom, my dear, dear son Absalom! Why couldn’t it have been me instead of you? My death for yours, oh Absalom, my dear, dear son!”

title: The King's Complicated Comeback
paragraphs: Joab got the news that David was basically a wreck, crying his eyes out over Absalom. So the day's huge victory felt more like a funeral because the word got out: “The king is grieving for his son.” The soldiers all felt super awkward and just snuck back into the city, totally demoralized. And the king was just hiding his face, wailing out loud,
“Oh, my son Absalom! Absalom, my dear, dear son!”

But Joab went to the king privately and was like, “Seriously? You just embarrassed all your loyal soldiers who literally just saved your life, not to mention your whole family. What’s up with this? You’re loving the people who hate you and hating the people who love you? You’re basically telling everyone that your team means nothing to you. You know, if Absalom was alive right now, we’d all be dead—is that what you wanted? Get it together, man. Go out there and encourage your troops. II swear to God, if you don't, they'll all ditch you by tonight.And that would be even worse than anything that’s happened before.”

So, the king finally got up and went to the city gate. The news spread like wildfire: “Hey, the king is out to see us!” And the whole army came and stood before him. Meanwhile, all the Israelites who had fought against David had run off and gone home.

Back in Israel, people were starting to complain to their leaders. “Yo, wasn’t it the king who saved us from all our enemies, like the Philistines? But then he had to run away because of Absalom. Now Absalom, the guy we made king, is dead. So what are we waiting for? Why aren’t we bringing the king back?”

When David heard what everyone was saying, he sent a message to the priests, Zadok and Abiathar. “Go ask the elders of Judah, ‘Why are you guys dragging your feet on bringing the king back home? You’re my own family, my flesh and blood! So why are you the last ones to do this?’ And say this to Amasa, ‘You’re my family too. I swear to God, I’m making you the new commander of the army instead of Joab.’”
He totally won over the hearts of everyone in Judah. They all agreed and sent a message to the king: “Come back, you and all your crew.”

So the king headed back. He got to the Jordan River just as the people of Judah were arriving at Gilgal to welcome him and help him cross. Even Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim who had cursed David, rushed down with a thousand Benjaminites to welcome the king. And Ziba, Saul’s old servant, showed up with his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They crossed the Jordan to meet the king and did everything they could to help him and his group.

As soon as he was across the Jordan, Shimei bowed down low in front of the king and said, “My lord, please don’t hold a grudge. Forget about the dumb stuff I said when you left Jerusalem. I know I messed up, but look, I’m the first one from all of northern Israel to come and welcome you back!”
But Abishai son of Zeruiah cut in, “Hold up! Shouldn’t we just kill this guy? He cursed God’s chosen king!”
David shot back, "Why are you sons of Zeruiah always trying to start something? No one is getting killed today. I’m king over Israel again!”
Then the king looked at Shimei and said, “You’re not going to die.” And he promised him.

Then Mephibosheth, Saul’s grandson, came from Jerusalem to welcome the king. The dude was a mess—he hadn’t washed his clothes, trimmed his beard, or combed his hair since the day the king left. When the king saw him, he asked, “Hey, why didn’t you come with me, Mephibosheth?”

He replied, “My king, my servant totally played me. I can’t walk, so I told him to get my donkey ready so I could go with you. But he just took off and then lied to you about me. But you, my king, are like an angel from God; you always know the right thing to do. My whole family could have been wiped out, but you took me in and gave me a seat at your own table. What more could I possibly ask for?”
“Okay, that’s enough,” the king said. “No more talking. Here’s my decision: you and Ziba will split the property.”
Mephibosheth said, “Honestly, let him have it all. All that matters to me is that you’re home safe, my king.”
Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim to see the king off across the Jordan. He was eighty years old and had been supplying the king with everything he needed while he was in Mahanaim.
“Come to Jerusalem with me,” the king told Barzillai. “I’ll take care of you there.”

But Barzillai was like, “How much longer do I even have to live? I’m eighty years old, man. I can’t taste my food, I can’t hear music… why would I be anything but a burden to you? I’ll just walk with you a little way across the Jordan. You don’t need to make a big deal out of it. Just let me go back to my hometown to die and be buried with my parents. But here’s my servant, Kimham. Let him go with you, and please treat him well.”
“Deal,” said the king. “Kimham will come with me, and I’ll treat him great. And if you need anything else, just let me know.”
So the army crossed the Jordan, but the king stayed behind for a minute. He kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and then Barzillai went home. Then the king and Kimham crossed over to Gilgal.

The whole army of Judah and half of the army of Israel were with the king. But then the men of Israel came to the king and said, “Hey, why are our brothers from Judah acting like they own you, sneaking you and your family across the Jordan?”
The men of Judah shot back, “Because the king is our relative, that’s why! Why are you making a big deal out of it? It’s not like we’re getting special treatment.”

The men of Israel were like, “We have ten times the stake in the king that you do! And we’re the older brothers, so why are you treating us like we’re second-class? It was our idea to bring him back in the first place!”
But the men of Judah just got even more aggressive in their response.

title: Sheba's Failed Rebellion: Don't Mess with David's Crew
paragraphs: Just then, this total troublemaker named Sheba, son of Bicri from the Benjaminite crew, blew a horn and started shouting,
"We're done with David! There's no future with Jesse's son. Israel, let's bounce—everybody go home!"

So, all the guys from Israel walked away from David and went to follow Sheba son of Bicri. But the men of Judah were loyal, sticking with their king all the way from the Jordan River to Jerusalem. When David got back to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he'd left to watch the house and put them in a separate, guarded place. He made sure they had everything they needed, but he never visited them again. They were basically locked away until they died, living like widows even though their husband was alive.

The king told Amasa, "Get the men of Judah together for me in three days, and then report back." Amasa went to gather the troops, but he was running late. So David said to Abishai, "Sheba son of Bicri is gonna cause us even more trouble than Absalom. Take my best soldiers and hunt him down before he hides in a fortified city where we can't reach him." So, with Abishai in charge, all the elite fighters—Joab's men and the special forces, the Kerethites and Pelethites—left Jerusalem to chase after Sheba. They were near the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa showed up. Joab was in his uniform with a sword in its sheath at his waist, but the sword slipped out and fell. Joab walked up to Amasa and said, "What's up, bro?" and grabbed Amasa's beard with his right hand like he was going to give him a friendly kiss. Amasa didn't even see the sword in Joab's other hand. Joab stabbed him right in the stomach, and his guts spilled out onto the ground. He didn't need to strike him again; Amasa was dead. Then Joab and his brother Abishai kept chasing Sheba.

One of Joab's soldiers stood over Amasa's body and yelled, "Anyone who's with Joab and on Team David, follow Joab!" Amasa was just lying there in a pool of his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier saw that the whole army was stopping to stare, so he dragged Amasa's body off the road into a field and threw a blanket over it so people would stop gawking. Once the body was out of the way, everyone moved on, following Joab to hunt down Sheba. Sheba went through all the tribes of Israel until he got to a town called Abel Beth Maacah. All the Bicrites, his own clan, grouped up and followed him into the city.
Joab's army showed up and surrounded Sheba in Abel Beth Maacah. They built a huge ramp up against the city's outer wall, getting ready to smash it down.

But then, a really smart woman from inside the city shouted out, "Listen up, everyone! Can someone please tell Joab to come over here so I can talk to him?" When he got close, the woman asked, "Are you Joab?"
He said, "Yeah, that's me."
